Three fixes for the same underlying problem: the automator could end up with an
**older** file than the one it already had.

## A re-release could be overwritten by the release it replaced

One Pace's feed lists a new release alongside its predecessor, so the same
season/episode gets queued twice with different CRC32s:

| Episode | CRC32 | |
|---|---|---|
| Post-War 01 | `5DC550F9` | the new re-release |
| Post-War 01 | `E7B15590` | the older release the catalog still lists |

Both downloaded, and whichever finished last won — the import removes any other
file occupying that slot. Which release you ended up with was down to download
order. Worse, a stale row left in the pipeline meant **Retry failed** would
replace a good episode with an older one.

An import is now refused when the file already in the library is newer, using
the same test the coverage report uses: a CRC32 the dataset has never listed
came from a release that landed after the dataset was generated, so it is newer
than anything the catalog knows. The stale row is marked done against the file
that's already there rather than failing, so retrying is always safe.

## A qBittorrent outage failed every queued download

When the qBittorrent container — or a VPN sidecar like gluetun in front of it —
restarts, every completed download in the sweep throws `ECONNREFUSED`. That
marked the whole pipeline `failed` and fired a Discord alert per episode, for
what was a passing outage that said nothing about the episodes themselves.

Connection errors now leave the episode queued for the next poll and stop the
sweep instead of burning through the rest of the queue. Torrent cleanup after a
successful import is best-effort too — a hiccup there could previously flip an
episode that was already safely on disk to `failed`.

## Batch files ahead of the dataset were thrown away

A file like `[One Pace][252-254] Skypiea 08 [1080p][A1DFB514].mkv` was skipped as
"unresolvable" because the catalog hadn't listed that hash yet — but that is
precisely what makes it the *newer* file, so the library kept the stale
catalogued release and the better file sat in `/downloads` being re-skipped every
cycle. The arc and episode are now recovered from the filename, with episode text
pulled from the metadata sheet.

## Upgrading

Pull the image, then hit **Retry failed** once. Rows that failed on a connection
error re-download normally; rows holding a superseded release clear themselves
instead of downgrading; and any newer files already sitting in `/downloads` are
imported on the next completion.
